utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Before we hear the witness, are there any matters the parties would like to raise at this stage? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Hopefully briefly. I just wanted to point out some concerns I had with this witness out of the presence of the witness that have come up before in this case, and that is this witness directly states in his report that the indictment implies that Mr. Jokic is charged with command responsibility as a commander in relation to his engineering jobs and his duty officer job. He specifically states -- the indictment says that. And he in addition states that the Prosecution has argued that. And this was clearly the thrust of the Defence cross-examination as we were going through the Prosecution's case. Because of that, and I'm frankly not clear why that is argued, whether it's just miscommunication or confusion or an attempt to build the Prosecution's case into something it's not so you can knock it down. I don't know. I don't know what it is. But as you may recall in the Rule 98 -- in our Rule 98 response, we very clearly laid out that it is not the position of the Prosecution, it is not in the indictment that we are charging Mr. Jokic as a commander. And we tried to set that record clear. This witness spends much of his report arguing that Mr. -- that we say that he is a commander and arguing that he is not. And so it's really not relevant. However, it's a little more complicated than that and I know that. Because we do know and we have acknowledged that there has been some evidence that Mr. Jokic had more authority than would normally be set forth in the rules of the duty officer job and the engineer's job. That notably came from Mr. Obrenovic after his plea, and there is some other evidence indicating Mr. Jokic carried out some authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I got your point but do not argue your case at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to argue the Defence case, which perhaps I shouldn't either. But what I'm saying is I will not be objecting to cross-examination on that evidence, on that evidence that came out regarding his additional authority. That I think is perfectly relevant. It came out through Obrenovic and that's fine. But I -- why I says it's tricky is there is a difference between us saying he is a commander and having the witness argue all day that he is not and the witness suggesting that he doesn't have the authority. I don't mind, of course, any problem with any material that Obrenovic has said. And so you'll -- I will hopefully be quiet during that part of it. But this additional -- the Prosecution has charged him as a commander is irrelevant and is not true, and I think -- I know the Court understands the subtle differences and of course there are. In addition, I think the Court -- probably everyone noticed that this report spends a lot of time arguing the ultimate issue of -- it reads like a lawyer's trial brief in many respects. It comes out at one point and says that the -- based on the indictment and the evidence presented, the Prosecution has not proved the following beyond a reasonable doubt and is just incorporating all the facts. Now, that is not appropriate, as the Court knows, for an expert to do. And I don't wish to be -- to be in an argument with a witness over the case. Mr. Stojanovic and I will argue over that but -- and again there are fine lines between what an expert can testify and what he can't. But clearly this expert goes well beyond the bounds in his report. It's obviously so clear and I know the Court can recognise it. So I am not suggesting that his report not be admitted in evidence. I think the Court will give it whatever weight it deems necessary. But at this point, at the time of testimony, these are a couple of concerns that I have that I did not want to explain in front of the witness at the time of objections. So I -- and I've had a chance to talk with counsel a bit about this as well. So that's all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any response, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Yesterday afternoon we talked with Mr. McCloskey, and he did indicate to us that before we hear the witness he was going to address you, as he has done. I would like to thank him first of all for the fact that Mr. McCloskey today for the transcript confirmed that not for a moment does he claim that our client, Dragan Jokic, was in command. However, Your Honour, you know that from day one we have had a problem with the term "control," "rukovodjenje." The term "rukovodjenje," was used literally in every point of the indictment in which Dragan Jokic is mentioned. Your Honour, according to the rules, there is no control without command. Control is realised through command. And this is the problem that this Defence and in semantics we are encountering. For all this we had the testimony of the witness of the Prosecution, Mr. Obrenovic, who for the first time mentioned that at one point the commander of the brigade transferred the command authority over the engineering unit to our client, Dragan Jokic. That was the problem that we had and which we were facing. We say that Dragan Jokic did not control the engineering unit. In my questions which I have for the expert witness, I will focus on a different line not attempting at any moment to deal or defend that question of command. I hope that you understand me when I say what the problem of this Defence is, because when we defend command we also need -- when we defend control, we also need to defend command. There can be no control without command. We will keep in mind everything that you have said, but it was my duty and I was obliged to say what I have said. I also must say that this was a key problem in conceiving the defence of Dragan Jokic, who keeps insisting to me as his Defence counsel in proving the incorrect allegations stated by Mr. Obrenovic. We're using a lot of energy and investing a lot of energy in this fact on which Dragan Jokic is insisting, and we have received a response from the Prosecution now that he is not being charged with command, but this is our problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, today we are not debating the legal issues or factual issues whether your client is a commander or not. You know, this is not the subject matter that we are going to discuss about. We are going to discuss -- we are going to discuss about is the matter that the status of the experts that we are going to hear. From the report and from your submissions, we found that there is no clear indication that this expert is, in fact, an expert, although we have received the CV submitted by you yesterday. You know, the actual content of the report is not quite what one would expect from an independent expert. He also has made a number of the comments in those parts that the Trial Chamber may not wish to admit into the evidence. I believe that we have already made a decision concerning of the Prosecution's expert witness dated on the November 7th, 2003. We set out several criteria concerning of the status of the expert. If the coming witness meets those criteria, it could be regarded as an expert witness. But judging from the report of that expert, we somehow believe that he did not live up to that standard. There were several matters that I would like to mention, because it is clear the expert witness expressed his opinion and draw some conclusions. And some of the conclusions may be unfounded or uncalled for. In general, an expert report is expected to provide an objective view on the facts, but this report states that he knew your client personally. In this case, it might be a problem, and he also draws some conclusions to his knowledge of the character of your client. We believe that it is not that proper. The report also makes some conclusions on the legal issues. For instance, whether the transfer is forced or voluntary, whether the column is a civilian population or not, et cetera. This is the legal problems, legal issues. And also he made some conclusions on the issue of fact. I will not list all those facts, but you may find it in paragraphs 73, 89, and 133. Another matter is that this report draws some conclusions on the state of mind of different people. We were told that he is an expert witness not a psychologist, but he made some assumptions on the state of mind of your client and other people. And last, he draws some conclusions of the judgement. In his report he clearly stated that there is either no or not enough evidence to prove beyond a reasonable doubt about your client's guilt. This is the conclusion. This is the legal matters not from the perspective of an expert. Without a strict description of the specific areas of the expertise of this witness the Trial Chamber may wish to consider not to admit this expert -- this report into evidence. That is, in the Chamber's view there were too many remarks, comments, and assumptions so far that seemed unfounded. So, Mr. Stojanovic, you may call this witness as a live witness, as an ordinary witness, and you could ask some questions, all those questions, to this witness. But in our view, he failed the criteria of being an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. I will try through my questions to get from the expert the interpretation for military regulations which regulate this question, and we will not ask the military expert for any conclusions as to the application of the cited regulations, but only what it stated in these regulations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, just -- if I could suggest -- it's going to be very difficult for this witness to be able to follow a script that is different from the one that he is prepared for. And it might save some time if Mr. Stojanovic had ten minutes to speak to him to tell him what the relevant subject matter is about and that is what he would be asking about. Because I don't think there is any deviousness going on here. I think they've prepared for him to be what he is, which as you've pointed out is improper. But I think if we can now prepare for him just briefly to talk about the appropriate issues, that would save time and hopefully keep me from having to object. Because the witness will not understand suddenly a change in course, I don't think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I see Mr. Karnavas is going to join the debate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I apologise. I don't mean to interfere here. But if I understand the Court correctly, the Court is not satisfied that a sufficient foundation has been laid to deem this person as an expert. That is, having special knowledge in a particular field that would make him an expert. And if I understand the Court correctly, the Court is not saying that he is not necessarily an expert but on its face it is unclear. So if perhaps a proper foundation was laid by Mr. Stojanovic by asking the requisite questions, and assuming that that meets the test, then perhaps he may be able to render certain opinions with respect to some very limited areas to the expertise. I believe that's what I understand the Trial Chamber is saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, frankly speaking, we are not satisfied with the report submitted by this expert witness. And the scope is -- in this report is very broad. There are two ways to deal with this matter: One is still regarding him as an expert witness but he will testify on very limited areas; secondly, we should regard him as an ordinary witness. The Defence counsel could ask him some broader issues concerning with his relationship, his judgement about Mr. Jokic and as well as some other things. Because he is just an ordinary witness like we heard before. These are two approaches that we could provide the parties to consider it. But anyway, that report could not be regarded as an expert report at all. The Bench is not ready to admit that report into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Perhaps, as Mr. McCloskey indicated, a ten-minute break may be appropriate. But getting back to the report, and I don't mean to quarrel. I have read the report. Obviously it does at some points invade the province of the Bench by forming some legal conclusions, but perhaps if -- there may be portions in the report that might be relevant, that might be highlighted. So the report doesn't necessarily have to be thrown out completely. But in any event, I think if Mr. McCloskey's suggestion could be granted, then perhaps the Defence of Mr. Jokic could regroup, and I might be able to provide a couple of suggestions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- yes, Mr. Stojanovic. We have spent a lot of time. Yeah, please be as concise as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. If you permit me just a little bit of time so that I could sit down with Mr. McCloskey and so that we can look at those parts of the report which have the nature of an expert report which pertain to the regulations relevant to the topics that we are dealing with. And then we can perhaps redirect and reorganise these questions so that our expert today can then be called as an expert for a limited number of questions which we would put to him today. It would be quite brief then, and it would only be the limited number of questions which we have already provided to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey. Very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I, of course, will speak to Mr. Stojanovic, but I'm hoping that we can -- that you will release him to speak to the witness as well, because that's the key thing. But there is also one other -- I think an important detail, and it may just be a translation issue, but if it is it is an unfortunate one, because Mr. Stojanovic has just mentioned that the key crux of their concern here was the term "control," as used in the indictment. We've just looked at it. The term "control" is not used in reference to Mr. Jokic in the indictment; it's used in reference to command of authority of Mr. Obrenovic. And the word "direct" is used in the area of the staff officer. So perhaps there's a translation issue, but we can try to sort that out as well, but it seems so fundamental to what they're saying that it needs to be sorted out, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the indictment has been issued for about four years and the trial has been going on for more than one year, then suddenly we find some problems. I'm surprised to hear that. I hope that issue could be ironed out, out of Court. Well, are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise? Could we go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We're working on that trying to develop whether we have evidence for rebuttal. Right now there are a few small points that we are interviewing some witnesses on and that we hope will be able to come in through 92 bis, because they are small rebuttal issues, and not many, frankly. And as for major issues of rebuttal, I don't see any major witnesses. The one witness that stands out as an issue for scheduling would be Witness 130. And that witness, while it has some rebuttal qualities to it, it would largely be a motion to reopen the case as we've discussed before. And I think there was differing views on the Defence part. But we are continuing to work with that situation and that witness to determine the best possible way to go on it. And I certainly expect to have something resolved, I hope, before the summer break, but we're -- it's a complicated issue. And -- but I believe we will be moving to reopen our case to have that witness testify. That's the direction we're going in. And -- but as I say, it's complicated. But that is our general plan right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If you have any motion for evidence in the rebuttal, I believe that the deadline will be the 26th of August, 2004, Thursday. As for the reopening of the case, that's another situation and you have to inform us as soon as possible if you have made up your mind, but no later than the 26th of August. Mr. Karnavas, do you have any --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just have one matter to raise with respect to the reopening of their case. The whole purpose - I assume - that they want to reopen the case is so that they can then say now you have to reconsider your judgement from the 98 bis motion. That's why I think it would be improper to ask for the reopening. The reopening would be only if they intended to go into areas that they failed to go into earlier. It would seem to me from reading 130's testimony that much of it is for rebuttal. So of course he has some additional information. We would not be objecting to that additional being introduced during the rebuttal phase, but I don't see that as a reason for reopening the case and then inviting a whole new set of motions as to the Court's reconsideration of its 98 bis. So I just want to say that. Secondly, Witness 130 mentions one particular individual who happens to be in custody in the United States waiting -- because of immigration problems. I spoke with the lawyer yesterday. I'm trying to make arrangements to see whether I need to go there and actually meet with this particular person, this individual, who is being held in custody to determine whether we're going to have to bring him in to rebut the rebuttal witness, 130. So I'll keep in touch with Mr. McCloskey on these issues, but that's going to be critical for us as well. I haven't made any concrete steps to meet with the gentleman, but I have spoken with his lawyer, and I know that the person is in the federal prison system in Arizona.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I tend to agree with you concerning the reopening of the case or rebuttal procedures, because the two procedures have two different practice and meanings of that. If it could be used as a rebuttal rather than reopening, that will be the best, but we'll let the Prosecutor decide. And if you have any rejoinder evidence, the deadline is September 2nd, Thursday, a week later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The same is true for Mr. Stojanovic. If you have any rejoinder submissions, the same deadline will apply to you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- and I believe that during the week of September 13th, 2004, if there is any rejoinder and rebuttal evidence, we'll begin the hearings. And all those witnesses in the rebuttal and rejoinder process should be very limited. It is not certainly the reopening of the case; it's just to certain areas or issues that the party has some problems with, but not the overall presenting your evidence. The final brief will be due on the 21st of September, 2004, for both parties. I would like to remind the parties that according to the rules the maximum length is 200 pages in total, including - including - the footnotes. On September 26th, Monday, we'll hear the closing arguments by the parties. I hope the closing arguments will be limited to one day for each party, because everything is there in the closing statement. And 30 minutes for each party for the rebuttal or rejoinder argument, if there are any. The Chamber will make a written decision to this aspect. There are two issues that still remain undecided. The first one is the time for Mr. Blagojevic's testimony, if there is any, if there is any. (Redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If there is nothing else, we'll make a break and we'll resume at 10.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. I think I should ask Mr. Stojanovic first, but since you already are standing up you may have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise. I was just spoken to by a representative of the translation booth, and apparently there has been a discussion about the proper translation of the terms "direct" and "control," and apparently there may be a difference between the Defence thinks it should be interpreted and the way the booth does. That's all I know about it, but again I don't know what was said with translations by the Defence. But perhaps they can clear it up. Because this witness will be using these sorts of terms and the translation needs to be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But no matter how it is translated, if we have the agreement of the meaning of the word, I think it's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just want to say I have absolute faith the translation booth has got it right, but apparently there may be a concern that the Defence has. I've heard that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, first of all you have to tell me about your discussions with the next witness. Secondly, you know, about these terminology issues. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We have spoken to our military expert. Before that, we agreed with Mr. McCloskey on the areas to be covered by this expert, namely military regulations. And we also raised this issue. I do not wish to exaggerate or to labour a point or to waste your time, but I have to tell you, Your Honour, that we have been dealing with this issue since we first objected to the indictment. This may be a semantic issue, but it may also go to the essence of the case. My knowledge of English is not good enough, so I may be wrong. But I will try to explain this very briefly. The concept -- I don't think I will have a problem, Your Honour, with respect to interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, my suggestion is that after the sitting you might have contact with the translation booth and discuss this issue in detail. As you said, it may be just a matter of translation and it might be related to some substantial issues. But I hope that we could have this issue solved before your case is over. So could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honour, while the expert is being brought in I wish to say something because this issue might come up during the expert testimony. I know that my defendant is not charged with command. This is not mentioned in the indictment. In my language there can be no command without "rukovodjenje." In my language the word "direction" cannot exist without implying control. In one of the indictments we received, Your Honours, the Prosecutor explained what they understand by the term "rukovodjenje," direction. And in count 46.4, or rather, paragraph 46.4 of the indictment it is stated that under rukovodjenje, that is direction, the Prosecution implies planning, monitoring, organising, and execution. These are all segments of command and therefore of "rukovodjene," direction. This is our problem, but I hope that it will not be an issue today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think your position is registered in the transcript, and I will repeat what I said that after the sitting you might have a meeting with the interpreters, if possible, as well as with Mr. McCloskey on these issues, yes. But we have a witness waiting and could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we are very flexible with the breaking time. Now you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stojanovic. I hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dragosav Lackovic, a colonel of the Army of Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, would you please spell your first and last name for the record, because we have a problem with one letter of your name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is D-r-a-g-o-s-a-v without an "l" in it. My last name is L-a-c-k-o-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lackovic. Would you please tell us when and where you were born.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 25th of September, 1961, in Bogatic in Serbia on the territory of the present state of Serbia and Montenegro. This is near a larger town called Sabac in the geographical region known as Maceva [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us briefly what your education and career was.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I completed primary school in the village of Klenje, which is close to Bogatic where I was born and where my parents live. On completing elementary school, I was admitted to the secondary school for army in Sarajevo. I went to school in Sarajevo for two years, and after this when I opted for engineering I continued my education in Karlovac. In 1980 I completed the military secondary school. After this, I was admitted to the military academy which I completed in 1983. And by my own wish, I was assigned to the engineering units of the then-air force and anti-aircraft defence. My first post was in the Ladjevci garrison near the Ladjevci airport near Kraljevo. In this unit, in engineer's battalion, I remained there until 1995. From that unit I applied and was accepted for schooling in the Command Staff Academy of the Yugoslav army, which I attended and successfully completed from 1994, with some interruptions because of the wartime events in the neighbourhood, until 1996. In this unit, I'm referring to the engineering battalion in Ladjevci, this was an independent engineering unit, I assumed all the duties ranging from komandir of the engineers' platoon all the way up to deputy commander of the independent battalion. After graduating from the command staff school, due to the needs of the service, I was reassigned to the Pancevo garrison, where I spent commanding the independent engineering battalion. I stayed there until 1998. From 1998 until 2001, due to the needs of the service, I was chief of engineers in the command of the air force corps. In 2001, again because of the needs of the service, I was reassigned and became the commander of the 305th Engineering Brigade, and this is the highest level such unit in the Army of Serbia and Montenegro. At the same time I was the commander of the Sabac garrison, and this was a special pleasure for me, because it is, conditionally speaking, my native town. In 2002 -- there's a technical problem? In 2002 I applied and was accepted to the National Defence School, the highest school in the military education system in Serbia and Montenegro. I graduated with honours in 2003, and after this, due to the needs of the service, I was assigned to the duty of deputy commander of the Belgrade military district. And I am still holding that post today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lackovic. Does this mean that practically your entire professional military career has been spent in the engineers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Most of my professional military career was in the engineers. I have already pointed out that I held all command posts in the engineers ranging from platoon commander to commander of the engineering brigade. There is no higher ranking duty in the engineers. In parallel with this, I also held several staff posts, both in the engineering units and in the command of the air force corps while I was chief of engineers in the staff of the air force corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lackovic. At the moment when we first met and when I asked you to write an expert report on the regulations which regulate the duties of the chief of engineers in a brigade and the duties of the duty operations officer in a brigade, that is the regulations which were in effect in 1995. Would you say that the regulations of the former JNA were applied in June 1995 in the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There's no foundation that this witness has any knowledge of the Republika Srpska army. We have seen other evidence regarding that, but this witness is not been -- there's been no foundation that he knows a thing about the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have heard some evidence on this aspect. I believe that all the persons who is working or serving in that army have some knowledge about that. We'll allow this question. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, let me just repeat. The regulations of the former JNA, according to your knowledge and according to your experience, were they applied by the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. As far as I know all the regulations that were used by the former JNA were also applied by the units of the Army of Republika Srpska. There were some more specific documents which, according to my knowledge, were based on the original documents which were then in use by the JNA. There were some internal recommendations and guidelines which came about because there was a need to explain some of the rules that dealt with the issues that existed in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I wanted to deal with some issues today, those issues refer to the application of the regulations that concern the duties of the duty operations officers and the chief of engineers. In other words, I wanted to ask you several questions regarding the regulations regulating these duties. Mr. Lackovic, we have often met with the term "resubordination" here. Can you please tell us: Is this a military term? What does it refer to? What does it imply, bearing in mind the regulations that were in effect in the Army of Republika Srpska. When we use the term "resubordination," what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. Resubordination is a customary military term which may be often heard. Its explanation can be found in a military lexicon and a military encyclopedia. Resubordination, in simple terms, could be explained as taking parts of one unit and joining that part with some other unit which is under the command of the same officer, and this is done specifically for the execution of a specific mission or task. In order to be more precise and more clear, let me illustrate this by an example. When we say "resubordination," we imply such a procedure by which the brigade commander takes people from one battalion, takes one company from one battalion, and joins it to another battalion for the execution of a specific task. So this company is added to that battalion in order to perform a task. In that, this unit, the unit which was taken from the original unit and added to the other unit as a rule, is at least one grade lower than the unit to which it is resubordinated. Resubordination in legal terms also means the transfer of command duties to a different, to a new, commander. And this new commander has the right to command this newly attached or resubordinated unit. The only thing that he can't do is carry out personnel changes in that unit. On completion of that task, the unit goes back to its original battalion from which it was taken and attached to a different unit unless there is a different order, an order to a different effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you for a moment. Can you please explain what you mean when you say that a new commander - and I repeat, a new commander - has the right to command the resubordinated unit? What do you mean when you say "new commander"? Who is the one who is -- who has the right to command this resubordinated unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, from the moment a unit is resubordinated - and I will explain, I will explain the moment when that happens - the commander to whom this unit is resubordinated has the right to command that unit. And I am referring to the commander of that battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I object to the relevance of this. I'm not aware of anything in this case where this is an issue, really with commanders and units now. If this is in the context of the duty officer, then I think that's relevant. But all this other stuff I don't see the relevance of at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, maybe you could ask some questions to this witness to establish the relevancy of his testimony to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Should you believe that this is not up to this expert to explain this and that he is talking about facts, I will do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, we have heard a lot of testimonies here about the situation in which Dragan Jokic as chief of engineers of the Zvornik Brigade sent members of the engineering company together with a vehicle to the civilian protection of Zvornik. And he himself returned to Bratunac on the order of civilian protection, and there again on the order of civilian protection, he performed duties which according to the Prosecution incriminated him. In keeping with the regulations that you were referring to, at the moment when the equipment and the troops of one brigade are attached to the civilian protection or any other unit and when they receive orders from that other unit, as you have just explained, are they resubordinated or are they not? Who is it who directs or commands the equipment and the troops that have left one brigade to be attached to another?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. From the moment when an individual reports to a certain officer or a commander of a unit to which troops were sent to reinforce that unit or to be resubordinated to it, from that moment onwards their engagement, their work, their disciplinary and other responsibility is something that is the responsibility of the officer to whom they have been resubordinated until the moment when this resubordination is finished. That is when that group of soldiers returns to their original unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Within the context of what you have just been talking about, according to the indictment Dragan Jokic on that day, the 14th of July, was the duty operations officer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Now we're going into specific facts in the indictment. We have no objection to the evidence of subordination, though I don't think he dealt with it in his report nor do I have any indication that it was going to be dealt with in his testimony. But it's a standard subordination. We agree. There's no -- nothing contested about that. How this Court may apply it to the facts that it's aware of is, you know, is fine, but to go -- to start quoting the indictment and have him judge the facts in the indictment in particular, that is not proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I agree with you on this point. Mr. Stojanovic, you may put your question another way. Maybe take a hypothetical example on that aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, let me ask you this: According to the regulations which were in effect in the Army of Republika Srpska, was it possible for a duty operations officer in any brigade to issue any type of orders to the members of that brigade about the use of that unit or for that unit to be sent to the area of responsibility of another unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Stojanovic. According to the regulations that were in effect then and are still in effect, duty operations officer was not given the authority to command or to decide on the combat use of either unit or their part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point we're going into that area that I spoke of. Nowhere in the Prosecution's case are we suggesting that he duty officer is a commander and initiating orders. The case is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So now we're going off into this area which is an area that is not -- it's not relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And it's not the area that he was supposed to be speaking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think there's no problem for the questions because the Defence asked the question that according to the regulations, what's the role of the duty officer? As an expert in the military sense, I think this witness will be capable to answer that question and which will be helpful to this Bench. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. With your leave, just one digression and then I will continue. The military analyst of the Prosecution has answered all these questions, and I want us to have the identical rights. Should I overstep that with our today's military expert, I will withdraw the questions. But these are the same and identical questions that the military expert that the Prosecution has called answered when he testified before this Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness should leave the room, Your Honour, but I feel very strongly about this issue. Mr. Butler never suggested a duty officer is a commander, and this is what this issue is going into. It's confusing. It's absurd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic [sic], we are not going to argue that issue in front of the witness. Here I believe Mr. Stojanovic just wants to tell us by asking some questions to this witness the role of the duty officer, at least in the interpretations of this witness. The questions in this area is allowed. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, let me ask you this: Which regulation regulates the duties, tasks, and authorities of the duty operations officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, these issues are regulated by the rule of service in the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do the rules that were in effect in July 1995 in the Republika Srpska army say? What do the rules say about the duties and the authorities of the duty operations officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try without quoting the rules to say briefly what the rules of service say about that issue. The rules of service regulate the way how the internal organs are appointed, how they're prepared for duties, how they're supposed to perform their duties, and very specifically what those duties are. I don't know what other specific things might interest you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the rules of service, is there a situation in which, in case there was no commander in the brigade command, the duty of command [as interpreted] would ever be taken by the duty operations officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: The regulations do not prescribe that the command role should ever be assumed by the duty operations officer. Whether this is hypothetically possible, whether this could happen in hypothetic terms, we're still in the realm of a hypothesis if such a thing should hypothetically happen. I would corroborate my opinion if you could allow me by showing you my position, and that is that experience and less experienced officers are appointed to be duty operations officers in the command. So it may occur that the duty operations officer for the day is an assistant commander, but also it can be a lower ranking officer in the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Allow me just this question: If there -- if the commander is not in the brigade command, according to the rules who stands in for him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: This is clearly regulated. When the commander is absent from his unit, his duties are assumed by the highest-ranking officer in the command, which is the Chief of Staff. If the Chief of Staff is not there, then it is the next officer, again the highest-ranking officer, who is there at the time. And that is one of the commander's assistants. In practice - and this has been supported by certain solutions that I could explain - it is most often the assistant command for logistics, because in the command hierarchy this officer is the third ranking officer in every command. Maybe we could illustrate this by saying that during the command [as interpreted] duty and the command of battle operations in the area of responsibility of one brigade, command posts are established. This is regulated by the instruction on the work of command staffs. Those command posts can be the basic, the reserve, the forward command post, and the rear command post. I'm saying this to corroborate my position that the assistant commander for logistics as the third ranking person in the command also has these duties established by the rules, because depending on the situation in the area of combat operations - and in this specific situation, in the area of the defence of the brigade - every of these command posts [as interpreted] can have more or less significance. It can be more or less important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just interrupt you for a brief moment. Mr. Lackovic, we have heard a number of military personnel and military experts who have testified and who have said that within that system the position of the chief of education [as interpreted] would be the third ranking position in the command. What is your position once you have familiarised yourself with the rules that regulate this issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sorry. We must have a translation issue because it got translated of chief of education, and I'm not aware of any such position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I also have some problems with this terminology. Mr. Stojanovic, would you please repeat that word.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It must be an interpretation problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, we have heard that the position of chief of operations and training is the third ranking position. What do military regulations say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. The duty of assistant of the commander for the operations and training in the brigade is the duty that you, I suppose, are talking about. It is correct that this duty is extremely important and that the department for operations and training and its chief are very important in the command structure, because by definition and according to the rules the complete analytical process based on the information received by the command is carried out in the department for operations and training. And it is not impossible to foresee a situation that the assistant commander for operations and training, in the absence of the first, second, and the third person, or the two persons - I'm referring to the commander and the Chief of Staff - so it is not impossible to foresee a situation in which this person could assume the command duties in the brigade. Because that person would obviously have a lot of information that might be of assistance to him to perform the command duties successfully. However, it is not very probable if there are any other assistants in the command, because this is what the rules say. The rule of the combat use of any unit amongst which the rules for applicable to the command say that the brigade commander is replaced by the highest-ranking officer in the brigade on the condition that the commander did not expressly appoint a different person that would stand in for him in the case of his absence. Based on the rules and regulations, I claim that -- more specifically in the command of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, in the absence of Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic and Major Obrenovic, according to the rules of the brigade, the highest and the most senior officer in the brigade was captain first class assistant commander for logistics. Milosevic was his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to focus on a couple of questions pertaining to the functioning of the forward command post. A little bit earlier you mentioned this term "forward command post." What do the regulations say? When is such a post formed, and is there a duty officer at the forward command post and do the duties of the duty officer in the command of the brigade and the forward command post overlap?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's a multi-part and really impossible for the witness to answer it like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It's a compound question. You may break your question piece by piece, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, could you please tell us: When is a forward command post formed and what is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said that according to the rules, principally in the manual for the work of command staffs and the rule on the use of the brigade, define or allow for the possibility for the commander to decide and to form a forward command post. Which conditions should be there or the combat situation in order for a forward command post to be formed, that depends on the assessment of the commander. But in any case, if the combat situation in the defence area of the unit is such that it calls for immediate and direct participation and monitoring of the situation on the ground directly on the location where everything is happening, then a forward command post is formed as a rule closer to the units which are involved in combat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, based on the documents that you analysed, do you know if in the area of the Zvornik Brigade in mid-July 1995 - and I'm specifically interested in the 14th and 15th of July, 1995 - there was a forward command post that was established?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. In the area of defence of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, a forward command post was formed or established in the sector of Kitovnice. And I'm saying this based on the information that I acquired based on the research.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a duty operations officer function at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. The forward command post has an internal service that is organised in the same way that it is organised at the command post. This includes all the other organs of the internal service, but until it is established it's a little bit reduced in size. In any case, it includes the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the authorities and the tasks of the duty officer at the forward command post identical to those of the duty officer in the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. The duties are identical, and they are laid down in the rules of service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In an -- in a forward command post that has not been established yet is the internal service being formed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is formed. An internal duty service is formed whose task, amongst other things, is to provide -- or to secure the actual command post and to prepare it for its full operations whereby it would have fully operational organs. So they are an organ of preparation. So when the need arises, then the forward command post can become operational immediately without any other preparations. The necessary communications are set up in order to command the units along the depth as well as other elements are set up which are believed to be essential once this becomes necessary. The elements are inactive, though, up until the time the command post becomes functional and begins to carry out its tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. For those of us who are not soldiers, sometimes it is difficult to understand what it means to take up a forward command post. From which point on can we consider the forward command post to be taken up? When does it begin to function?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, it is believed, according to the rules, that the command post is taken up at the point when the line of command is started to the subordinated units. From the point in time when the commander arrives at the forward command post -- it is assumed that he will not arrive by himself but he will come with certain equipment and personnel which are essential for him to carry out his function of command. So from that point on it is considered to be a forward command post that is active, that is taken up. Until they begin to work from that forward command post, the command post is not functional, it is not taken up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next question follows on logically. From which command post is the command carried out once the forward command post is taken up? What is the central point from which direction is carried out? So where is the place where the direction is actually carried out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Vague, Your Honour. I mean, in what context? We're talking peacetime, we're talking wartime, we're talking a campaign, a non-military campaign. I -- it's such a massively broad question and so fact-specific I would think, depending on the situation on the ground that I don't see where we're going with this in terms of relevant area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- yes, Mr. Stojanovic, I'm not a military expert, so I have some difficulties to understand your question. So you maybe have it rephrased or be more specific in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, let's go step by step. According to your research at one point in 1995 was a forward command post taken up within the command of the Zvornik Brigade, in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that the commander or the person substituting for him at that point was practically situated and directing the unit from the command post?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. That is the function of the forward command post, and that person is at the forward command post. And that command post is the main command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, at that point in time do orders and the direction of subordinated units flow from that forward command post?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... about the facts of the case. I think this witness is not qualified to say where the commander was and where orders were coming from, especially with such a general case where the command post -- well, I won't get into the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think this is an issue that the Chamber is interested to know. If you have some objections or questions concerning this aspect, you may raise it in your cross-examination. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, which command post becomes the central point for the direction of operations and combat operations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: The central or the main command post is the one post where the commander is or the person representing the commander when he's absent from the combat operations zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to take you back to a, let's say, theoretical question. Do the duties of the duty operations officer in the brigade change then? Does the level of his responsibilities and duties change? Is it increased or reduced?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Stojanovic. His duties remain unchanged, but his responsibility in any case in that context can be diminished because the scope of his duties can be reduced. But in any case, his responsibilities remain the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would orders to subordinate units then, or the use of subordinate units, the direction of subordinated units, go through the duty operations officer in the brigade or through the duty operations officer at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: According to the rules, Mr. Stojanovic, the information first goes to the place where the commander is and then to all the other subjects in the process of command. So information about the situation and the course of combat operations go to the commander if he's at the forward command post, if the forward command post is taken up. They go there first, to the place where the commander is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In that sense I will be finishing with that topic. This information coming to the commander as a central figure, did they have to come via the command post of the brigade and the duty operations officer who is conveying all this information to him, or are there any other systems for the commander to receive information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: I've already said, Mr. Stojanovic, that the forward command post has all the communications that the command post itself has, as well as some other facilities required for the direction of units during combat operations. So I think that the answer to your question would be that all information flow to the forward command post through those channels of communication. In practice, it is the case - most often - that most of the information does not go to the main command post, because that is not essential for the command and control of combat operations. But it is also possible that some of this information goes through other means of communication to the other organs of the command, primarily to the department for operations and training of the command of the brigade which can be at the basic or main command post as well as the forward command post. These are all parallel systems of communication. When we're talking about these systems of communications, the most important ones are the systems of command communications and the system of communications of duty operations officers. So the command line and the duty operations line. These two lines should not be mixed up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to move to another topic where I would like to ask for your help. We have often encountered the term here mobilisation of materiel facilities or means from the business community or the civilian community. As an expert in that area, could you please tell us which rules regulate the question of requisition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. There's been no foundation that he has any expertise in this area. I'm sure a couple of questions could get us there, but there should be at least a couple. I mean, what experience have you had in the mobilisation of materiels in your career. I mean, something. We don't even know if this man has any combat experience yet. He's talking about combat. So we need a few foundational questions. There's been no foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, you may ask some foundational questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, when describing your career at one point you said that during the wartime events and the attacks of the NATO air force against Serbia and Montenegro you performed command duties in an engineering unit. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: What period exactly are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When preparing for defence from the then-imminent threat of intervention by the NATO pact against the then-federal Republic of Yugoslavia, I was the commander of an engineering unit, but as of October, late October or early November, I was already in the staff of the air force corps. I performed both duties. During the NATO aggression, I was the chief of engineers in the corps. So that during the preparations I was the commander of an independent engineering battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did these preparations imply the need to requisition certain equipment and materiel which the army did not have at one point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, yes. Especially while preparing to take up a scattered disposition over the territory and we did not have sufficient transport capacity to do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When preparing for this expert testimony, did you come across regulations that were in force in the Army of Republika Srpska in 1995 regulating requisitioning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These were for the most part the same regulations applied in the former SFRY, later adopted by the SRY and the Republika Srpska. There are no material differences in the manner of carrying out mobilisation of manpower and requisitioning of equipment and materiel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could one say that you have both theoretical and practical experience in applying these regulations in the area of mobilisation and requisitioning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: I am familiar with the regulations, and I have personal experience to the extent I have described as the commander of a unit until October 1998, not later than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what the procedure is when requisitioning materiel for a unit if the unit does not possess a certain type of machinery or equipment or other types of materiel.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: My Stojanovic, by way of introduction to my response to your question, I would like to draw a clear distinction. Something like this happens very rarely because mobilisation and requisitioning is a process that entails planning, and the planning starts in peacetime. It entails undertaking measures and activities in order to achieve a certain level of combat readiness and to raise the manpower levels of the units to its full -- for purposes of war. If the planning has been done properly in accordance with the establishment of a certain unit and its needs, then there is no need for subsequent mobilisation or requisitioning. I assume your question refers to subsequent mobilisation or requisitioning. However, such a mobilisation or requisitioning cannot be excluded. If in spite of the fact that mobilisation has already been carried out it transpires that other equipment and materiel are required for the unit, in this situation the immediate user expresses his need for such equipment in his briefing to the commander. The commander then orders his assistants for mobilisation and -- or his Chief of Staff, and on the basis of this order, the assistant or Chief of Staff fills in a form which he sends to the Ministry of Defence which has the authority to provide certain equipment and materiel, provided that such equipment or materiel exists in the territory in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us which regulation provides for this.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: The rules on mobilisation which were in force in Republika Srpska at the time. But there were also other regulations by the state organs which provided for all of this in greater detail covering all the participants in the mobilisation process, including state organs, companies, and all other entities, because the process of mobilisation is a strategic activity of enormous importance for the state. As such, it is up to the state to carry out this job. But in order to make it operational some of the tasks are delegated to lower level organs and the process is simplified, conditionally speaking, but again in accordance with the rules and regulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me conclude by putting a specific question to you. In an infantry brigade, let's say an engineer's company needs certain equipment which it does not have. This equipment exists in a commercial company in a municipality, or rather, the municipality where this unit has its headquarters. Who has to submit a request and who would the process look like actually in this case?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I think I've just explained. But in this specific situation -- well, there are actually two situations that can occur. One situation is when the komandir, the commander of a company, receives a task from the brigade commander and then he asks the brigade commander to requisition certain equipment. In that case he will order the Chief of Staff to draw up a request form -- a requisition form, he will sign it and then send it off to be dealt with. So that this goes to the regional Ministry of Defence office. The second possibility is during the planning and preparation stage for the carrying out of certain engineering tasks, or engineering support for combat activities, the chief of engineers establishes that something should be done and proposes this to the Chief of Staff. The Chief of Staff transmits this proposal to the commander. The commander makes a decision and, again, orders that the requisition form be filled in, signed, and sent off. That's the procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point you said that it was possible for the chief of engineers to enter this whole process. What does the chief of engineers have to propose to the commander? What is his duty, his task, in all this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: It is the duty of the chief of engineers in the staff of the joint tactical units of the brigade, according to the rules on the use of engineers and the engineering support for combat operations, to propose what these rules provide for. The chief of engineers, that is, is an expert organ of the Chief of Staff. He participates in the process of preparing the commander's decision. He proposes to the Chief of Staff the way in which the subordinate engineering unit can be used in the most efficient and the best possible way and the best possible way that use can be made of the equipment available to the brigade. Also, he makes a proposal, if he feels it is necessary, as to what equipment should be left in the reserve and what the priorities should be in the engineering support to all the subordinated units. That is, what the engineering support should focus on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this may be a convenient moment for a break. I have just a few more questions in the domain of the tasks of the chief of engineers and the direction of an engineering unit, and then that would complete my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. How long do you think you need to finish the direct examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the break some 15 minutes or so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break, and we'll resume at five minutes past 11.00 -- past 12.00. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, we have left it off at the moment when we started talking about the duties of the commander of the engineering company and the commander of the brigade. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. But I believe that we haven't touched upon the duties of the commander of the engineering company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you as follows: During your professional career, did you perform the duties of the commander of the engineering company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, I did. I did perform the duties of the commander of the engineering company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also perform the duties of the chief of engineers in any of the units that you belonged to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the last bit because it wasn't recorded. Where did you perform the duties of the chief of engineers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: I performed the duties of the chief of engineers in the corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. According to the rules, who is it who directs the engineering company? Who is in charge of the direction of the engineers' company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Without my intention to speak about the definition of the term command, control, or direction or control, because in our theory it is different than the western theory of direction and organisation. It would be more appropriate for our situation to say commanding of a company. But in terms of your question, in any event, the officer who is in charge of directing and commanding a company is the company commander. It's his exclusive right, which is prescribed and found in the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which regulations regulated the issue of command and direction in an engineers company? What regulations are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Like any other duties and like in most military units, the duties of anybody is prescribed by combat rules. More specifically, when it comes to a company commander, the commander of an engineering company, I know that this is prescribed by the rules applicable to a company or a squad in the engineering unit. But also these duties stem from the rules of service in the armed forces relative to his role and relative to an officer of that rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commander of an engineering company, can he command and control an engineering company outside the context given to him by the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about the peacetime or the wartime functions, Mr. Stojanovic? What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was talking about extraordinary circumstances, wartime circumstances. The commander of an engineering company, can he be independent in issuing orders on the use and of a company that go beyond the orders of the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, as far as the combat use of an engineering company, the commander of that company is authorised to command the company in the spirit of the orders and decisions issued by his commander and nothing beyond that. In other segments, however, such as the combat training and preparations for the execution of missions and tasks, in other words, bringing all the strengths of the company up to the combat readiness ready to perform the future tasks is up to him. It is his personal matter, and in keeping with his training and with his determination, he can regulate it himself without any influence exerted on the part of the commander unless it is obvious that he does not do his job properly. Then the commander can correct his work and the ultimate correction can be the replacement of such a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the name of the document based on which the commander of the engineering company executes his duties of command and control?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: One of the combat documents which is used in the armed forces of the former JNA and Republika Srpska army is the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we talking about daily orders which are issued by the commander of the engineering company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about daily orders, but also in practice we have the so-called order of the company commander for the execution of a combat activity which may be either a defence or an assault or another technical duty. At this moment, it is not that important, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, tell us, please: In that system, where are the duties and tasks of the chief of engineers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand your question well, Mr. Stojanovic, the chief of engineers as a professional in the brigade command appears as such, and his role is decisive in the stage of planning of the future activities, either defence activities or assault activities or any other activity. In that stage, based on the information that he has about the subordinate engineering units and based on the basic ideas of the commander, on the way how the future tasks should be executed, he suggests or proposes to the commander. When I say "commander," I mean the Chief of Staff who will refer the proposal to the commander. Sometimes it may occur that this proposal reaches the commander directly, that he himself directly communicates to the commander. When I say "directly," that means that it can happen in a situation when the commander himself has requested that. After that, the commander will issue a decision. He will issue an order for a combat order to be drawn up, and that the plan of operations should be worked out. And he also issues orders to the subordinate units. Mostly it is done during the command inspection. The chief of engineers, in keeping with the proposal that has been adopted or the corrected proposal that has been adopted pursuant to the right of the commander to correct any proposal submitted to him, the commander may adopt the proposal in full. He may also alter it or change it or amend it, or he can also ask from the chief of engineers to correct the proposal himself, or to reject it completely for that matter, and to issue an order that things should be done the way he wants them to be done. This doesn't happen very often. However, this is the right vested in the commander. After that, the chief of engineers will work out certain documents if those are indispensable and necessary for the execution of the task in hand. And this is where his role in the process of decision-making mostly finishes. This is where his role is exhausted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lackovic, if there is a commander of the engineering unit, his deputy squad commander is in the engineering company, is there something in the rules that provides for the possibility for the chief of engineers to command and control the engineering unit?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the counsel uses the term "direction and command" of the engineering unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This possibility cannot be excluded. The chief of engineers may appear in the role of a person who will direct and command, or command and control the engineering company, although this happens very rarely in practice. However, it is not excluded. The brigade rules define this in the following way: The commander will issue a written order transferring his authorities to the chief of engineers in such a case. In practice, a different situation is more common, and this situation is also prescribed by the rules of combat used especially for light infantry brigade, such was the case in the Milic Light Infantry Brigade, for example. The company commander or the engineering unit commander is at the same time the chief of engineers. In that case, we may say that the chief of engineers is also the company commander. If the commander does not transfer his exclusive right of command by a written document on to an officer who will direct not only the engineering company but also any other unit, then this officer, whoever he may be, does not have the right command that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lackovic. We have heard this answer from Mr. Butler already, and Mr. Butler also said that he has not come across any written authorisation to transfer command. Let me ask you: During your analysis and dealing with your issue, have you encountered any written document by which the commander of the Zvornik Brigade has transferred his duties on to the -- on to a lower-ranking officer, on to the chief of engineers, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Stojanovic. I have not come across any such document by way of which the commander or in his -- or in the absence of Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic Major Obrenovic has transferred the duty of command to another person rather than the commander of the engineering unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let me finish by asking you this: According to the rules on subordination and the unity of command in the Army of Republika Srpska, was there any possibility for having two commanders commanding and directing one unit at the same time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if one was to respect all the rules and regulations to the letter, then this would be impossible. If you'll allow me, I would like to clarify. It is possible to have two individuals issuing orders. However, if we are talking about the command responsibility, only one person has the responsibility for command and that right will have been transferred on to him. Nobody else has that responsibility, and nobody in that unit is obliged to execute any such orders that would be given by anybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have asked this -- I have put this question to Mr. Butler. I would like to ask you the same. Why do you believe that this transfer of responsibility for command and control should be in written form? Why should it be in writing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSAV LACKOVIC
